tier_reason: The only numbers against a recognizable incumbent (MSXML 6.0) come from a competing vendor's README (maxdz mdz_xml) with the CPU (i5-6600) and toolset (VC++ v100 64-bit) stated but no optimization flags and no published harness, so not A; a closed-source competitor's table is not a well-known independent suite, so not B. TinyXML-2's own README has no figures, only 'efficient' and faster than TinyXML-1.

corrections.caveats: Weak evidence of an unusual kind: the numbers come from a competing commercial vendor (maxdz mdz_xml, closed source, evaluation binaries only, benchmark harness not published, optimization flags not stated) whose tables use public Wikimedia dumps from March 2021 and a TinyXML-2 snapshot of 23.03.2021, so they predate several major TinyXML-2 releases. In those tables TinyXML-2 is the slowest of the open parsers (RapidXML about 4.4x and pugiXml about 6.0x faster in raw parse at 800 MB, derived from page data), uses more memory than MSXML (5477.5 vs 3428.5 MB at 800 MB, 9601.6 vs 6095.3 MB at 1.5 GB) and crashes on the 2.0 GB and 2.7 GB files that MSXML parses. In the raw-parse table only the Parse() call is timed for TinyXML-2, while MSXML is driven through IXMLDOMDocument with its timed scope unstated, so the 1.7x raw-parse ratio may flatter TinyXML-2; the load-parse-unload tables (1.8x warm, 1.5x cold) are the fairer comparison. MSXML 6.0 is Windows-only, not libxml2. Other third-party data points go against it: the siximapala/XML-plugins-exhibit README sample CSV (0 stars, hardware and flags unstated, Windows build) has pugixml read 10 MB in 18-20 ms vs TinyXML2 65-102 ms and RapidXML 42-55 ms, and 200 MB in 328-562 ms vs TinyXML2 1226-1272 ms. tinyxml2 issue #52 'Benchmark?' (opened 2012, now closed) asked for a comparison with pugixml and received no numbers. The lead's guessed baseline (libxml2) has no TinyXML-2 numbers anywhere reachable.

notes: All numbers in claimed_speedup appear in the mdz_xml README tables and the derived ratios check out (1.74x and 1.74x raw parse, 1.77x and 1.78x warm, 1.51x cold). Shortcomings to record: only faster than MSXML 6.0 (Windows-only) in a competitor's unreproducible 2021 table, slowest of the open parsers there, higher memory than MSXML, crashes on 2.0 GB and 2.7 GB inputs, and unequal timing scope (Parse() only) in the raw-parse table. Metadata confirmed (Zlib, 5.8k stars, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-05-24); the libsimdxml exclusion claim in caveats was not re-checked (repo not found in one search), and pugixml.org/benchmark.html, which might include TinyXML-2, is EGRESS_BLOCKED.
